items.name: TACTO
items.summary: Configurable optical tactile rendering with perception and control demonstrations. The paper reports hundreds of frames per second in its tested setup.
items.implication: Compare optical accuracy and matched-workload speed; fast images alone do not establish a unique product.

items.name: Taxim
items.summary: Example-based GelSight optical response and elastomer marker-motion modeling calibrated from real sensor observations.
items.implication: Compare calibration cost and reserved-contact image/marker error; attribute reuse of its rendering model.

items.name: TacSL
items.summary: GPU visuotactile images and contact-force distributions with robot-learning tools and sim-to-real experiments.
items.implication: Use full-loop throughput and real usefulness under matched settings as comparison targets.

items.name: DiffTactile
items.summary: Differentiable tactile simulation combining an FEM sensing elastomer, multi-material mechanics, contact dynamics and optical response.
items.implication: Use as a mechanics and identification precedent; test whether a simpler approximation preserves useful accuracy.

items.name: HydroelasticTouch
items.summary: Pressure-based tactile sensor simulation using hydroelastic contact surfaces.
items.implication: Include a distributed-pressure baseline when evaluating contact-field fidelity.

items.name: HydroShear
items.summary: History-dependent shear and stick-slip tactile simulation with reported zero-shot RL transfer on specified physical tasks.
items.implication: A shear-centered product needs a measured advantage over this close prior art.

items.name: NVIDIA Isaac Lab visuotactile contribution
items.status: Current documentation labels visuotactile functionality experimental/contributed
items.summary: Camera RGB/depth and normal/shear tactile fields are documented, including Taxim-based optical rendering.
items.implication: Built-in tactile support is already present; validate a calibration, accuracy or workflow advantage.

items.name: Newton Physics
items.summary: Warp/OpenUSD physics ecosystem with pluggable solvers and documented SDF/hydroelastic contact paths.
items.implication: Keep contact and sensor interfaces portable; do not claim distributed contact is missing from platforms.

items.name: MuJoCo tactile sensing
items.status: Current native tactile and touch-grid documentation checked
items.summary: Touch-grid force aggregation is documented; former touch-stress plugin functionality moved into a native tactile sensor.
items.implication: Assess native sensing before implementing a custom layer; optical rendering and calibrated mechanics remain separate questions.

items.name: Drake hydroelastic contact
items.summary: Distributed contact surfaces and pressure fields with documented fallback and geometry limitations; hydroelastic contact does not introduce true deformation state.
items.implication: Use pressure and timestep baselines carefully; numerical hydroelastic parameters are not universally intrinsic material constants.

items.name: Genesis tactile sensors
items.status: Versioned tactile documentation and sandbox inspected
items.summary: SDF/point-cloud query probes provide approximate dense contact/taxel fields; the sandbox warns its readings are not calibrated.
items.implication: Dense fields need independent physical validation; do not treat a visualization's force label as a measurement.

items.name: SPOTS
items.status: Initial preprint 2023; revised 2026; journal acceptance stated
items.summary: Joint visual/tactile prediction studies the value of touch in physically ambiguous robot interactions.
items.implication: Choose experiments where physical information is difficult to infer visually; do not expect uniform gains everywhere.

items.name: RoboPack
items.summary: A learned tactile-informed dynamics model supports real manipulation and dense packing using real interaction data.
items.implication: Useful action-conditioned dynamics precedent; preserve the real-data training distinction.

items.name: TacForeSight
items.summary: Wrist force/torque conditions short-horizon tactile latent forecasts that provide anticipatory information to a manipulation policy.
items.implication: Inspect what future action/force information a predictor requires before treating it as a counterfactual simulator.

items.name: TACO
items.summary: Real rollouts feed a recognize-imagine-label loop that produces local visuotactile corrections for policy post-training.
items.implication: A concrete synthetic-data workflow is relevant, but it is not an entirely simulation-trained policy demonstration.

items.name: FeelWorld
items.summary: A hierarchical model predicts visual latents, contact, force-related tactile latents and slip, supporting contact-aware planning.
items.implication: Structured state and contact gating are useful comparisons; a tactile latent is not automatically a calibrated force law.

items.name: ContactWorld
items.status: September 2026 v3 checked; title updated from supplied report
items.summary: A controlled representation benchmark across contact-rich tasks, with current-source simulation and physical evaluation.
items.implication: Evaluate representation structure and downstream task benefit; do not describe the work as simulation-only.

items.name: Sparsh / TacBench
items.summary: Self-supervised optical-touch encoders and a downstream tactile benchmark across supported sensors/tasks.
items.implication: Compare perception heads using strong pretrained representations; no mechanics identification follows automatically.

items.name: AnyTouch / TacQuad
items.summary: Static/dynamic tactile representation learning uses aligned multi-sensor observations to study cross-sensor transfer.
items.implication: Sensor transfer is an explicit test axis rather than an automatic property of a shared encoder.

items.name: AnyTouch 2 / ToucHD
items.status: ICLR 2026 acceptance stated in primary record
items.summary: Force-aware dynamic optical-touch representation learning with atomic actions, manipulation and touch-force paired data.
items.implication: Audit actual channels, calibration and rights before choosing data for a force-transfer experiment.

items.name: ObjectFolder 2.0 / ObjectFolder Real
items.relationship: Complement / prior art for sensory assets
items.summary: Implicit multisensory virtual objects and measured real-object data support sight/sound/touch learning tasks.
items.implication: Touchable object assets have prior art; reusable calibrated material/contact laws need separate evidence.

items.name: Cluster Haptic Texture Dataset
items.summary: Controlled sliding texture recordings span velocities and directions; the sibling project uses a restricted vibration-spectrum task.
items.implication: Preserve local clock/channel limitations; spectrum prediction does not establish synchronized force or free-motion dynamics.

items.name: GelSight Mini
items.summary: Optical tactile sensor marketed for robotics/research with gel deformation images and software integration resources.
items.implication: Candidate first sensor family; confirm the user's actual device, outputs, calibration and bandwidth.

items.name: XELA uSkin / uAi
items.summary: Distributed three-axis tactile sensing with software for visualization, calibration and compensation.
items.implication: Hardware vendors already provide useful software; identify the remaining simulation or calibration pain precisely.

items.name: AnySkin
items.summary: Replaceable magnetic skin sensing and cross-instance generalization of learned models in specified experiments.
items.implication: Separate object/material transfer from replacement-sensor transfer; do not assume all pads are interchangeable.

items.name: RobotSweater
items.summary: Customizable machine-knitted pressure-sensitive skins with robot tactile-feedback demonstrations.
items.implication: Body coverage already exists in research; whole-body simulation needs heterogeneous sensor models and validation.

items.name: ChainQueen and differentiable mechanics
items.summary: Differentiable MLS-MPM mechanics supports deformable-body simulation and inverse/control optimization.
items.implication: Gradients support fitting but do not identify parameters without informative calibrated measurements.

items.name: Penn HaTT / LMT / STAG / tactile gloves
items.status: Named in supplied report or earlier local catalog; archives not re-audited in this update
items.summary: Candidate texture, human-pressure and demonstration resources may inform later sensing and observation studies.
items.implication: Confirm release schema, calibration, synchronized labels and commercial/redistribution terms before promising use.
